about.title: The person behind the engineering.
paragraphs: I'm Sebastian Ardila — a Senior Engineer and UX Director with {years}+ years building products that ship, scale and stay alive past the founder's first crisis.

I work at the intersection of architecture and design. I started in code, grew into leading teams, and learned the hard way that the best engineering decisions are the ones that protect a product's future, not the ones that look clever today.
I'm based remotely. I work with founders, agencies and tech teams who want a partner — not a contractor.
about.caption: Sebastian Ardila

pillars.title: Observe before you optimize.
pillars.description: Ship metrics before features. We instrument the system so every decision after week one is data-driven, not opinion-driven.

pillars.title: Reduce the cost of change.
pillars.description: Modular boundaries, typed contracts, deployable in fragments. Refactor becomes routine, not a quarterly event.

pillars.title: Compound, don't accumulate.
pillars.description: Tech debt is interest you didn't agree to pay. Each iteration leaves the codebase cheaper to extend than the last.

paragraphs: Software is a living system. It is never finished — it is maintained, observed, and improved. Every codebase carries a hidden interest rate; the engineer's job is to keep that rate low so the founder can keep investing in growth, not in repairs.
I don't believe in heroic rewrites. I believe in small, deliberate improvements that, compounded across years, separate companies that scale from companies that stall.
philosophy.signature: — That is Kaizen. That is the work.
